record.original_question: In the same setting, with N a large prime and H_2^+(N) the weight-2 newforms of level Γ_0(N) with even functional equation, can one prove a stronger lower-bound statement: that more than 50% of the central values L(f,1) are at least (log N)^(-A) for some fixed positive constant A?

evidence.quote: Problem B. Better still, show that more than 50% of the central values are larger than (log N)^-A for some positive constant A.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $N$ be a (large) prime number, and let $H_2^+(N)$ denote the set of normalized weight-$2$ Hecke newforms $f$ on $\Gamma_0(N)$ whose completed $L$-function $\Lambda(f,s)$ satisfies a functional equation $\Lambda(f,s) = +\Lambda(f,2-s)$ (i.e., the sign of the functional equation is $+1$, so the central value $L(f,1)$ is not forced to vanish for parity reasons).

For $f \in H_2^+(N)$, let $L(f,s)$ denote the associated automorphic $L$-function, with central point $s=1$.

Prove or disprove: there exists an absolute constant $A>0$ such that, as $N \to \infty$ through primes,
$$\#\{f \in H_2^+(N) : L(f,1) \ge (\log N)^{-A}\} > \left(\tfrac{1}{2} + \delta\right)\, \#H_2^+(N)$$
for some fixed $\delta>0$ (independently of $N$).

That is, show that strictly more than $50\%$ of the central values $L(f,1)$, as $f$ ranges over $H_2^+(N)$, are bounded below by $(\log N)^{-A}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The best known unconditional results give that at least 50% of such central L-values are nonzero. Going strictly beyond 50% with a quantitative lower bound of the form (log N)^{-A} is known to be intimately tied to ruling out Landau–Siegel zeros for real Dirichlet L-functions (work of Iwaniec–Sarnak and subsequent authors), and remains open.

status_evidence.title: The non-vanishing of central values of automorphic L-functions and Landau-Siegel zeros
status_evidence.snippet: Improvement over 50% with a lower bound on L_f(1/2) would imply the non-existence of Landau-Siegel zeros for Dirichlet L-functions of real primitive characters.
status_evidence.claim: Pushing the proportion strictly above 50% with a (log N)^{-A} lower bound is linked to the Landau–Siegel zero problem and is open.

status_evidence.title: Simultaneous nonvanishing of central L-values with large level
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) work continues to study nonvanishing proportions for central L-values at large level, indicating the basic >50% with quantitative lower bound remains an active open question.
status_evidence.claim: The problem remains an active subject of research.
